examples.ko: 이 영화는 전 세계에서 수억 명이 봤어요.
examples.en: Hundreds of millions of people around the world watched this movie.
I heard that painting sold for hundreds of millions of won.

examples.ko: 목성은 지구에서 수억 킬로미터나 떨어져 있어요.
examples.en: Jupiter is hundreds of millions of kilometers away from Earth.
Hundreds of millions of years ago, dinosaurs lived.
Hundreds of millions of fish live in the sea.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 수억 번 들어도 질리지 않아요.
examples.en: I never get tired of this song even after hearing it hundreds of millions of times.

explain: '수억 원', '수억 명'처럼 단위 앞에 바로 붙여요. 정확한 숫자는 모르지만 억이 여러 개 되는 아주 큰 수를 말할 때 써요. '수십', '수백', '수천', '수만'도 같은 방식으로 써요.

phrases.en: There are hundreds of millions of stars in the night sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: '명', '원' 말고 '개'에도 붙일 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It can attach to '개' as well as '명' and '원'.

phrases.en: Someone donated billions of won.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수억'보다 더 큰 수를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for numbers even bigger than '수억'.

phrases.en: Tens of millions of people have listened to this song.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수억'보다 작은, 천만이 여러 개인 수예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A smaller number than '수억', several ten-millions.

explain_en: It attaches directly before a unit, as in '수억 원' and '수억 명'. The exact number is unknown, but it is several hundred million. '수십', '수백', '수천', and '수만' work the same way.

examples.en: The shipyard's order amount has grown a lot this year.

examples.ko: 이번 계약 덕분에 수주액도 일 조 원을 넘었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to this contract, the order total also exceeded one trillion won.

examples.ko: 수주액은 작년보다 두 배 가까이 올랐어요.
examples.en: The order amount rose nearly double compared to last year.
The company announced its overseas order amount.
The order amount has dropped, so the employees are worried.
The bonus varies depending on the order amount.

explain: 주문을 받는 것은 '수주', 주문을 내는 것은 '발주'라서 둘을 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요. '수주액'은 주문을 받은 금액이고, 건설·조선·수출 같은 경제 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 동사는 '수주하다'예요.

phrases.en: Thanks to the new factory, the amount of orders increased.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주문을 받은 금액이 많아졌다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the amount of orders received has grown.

phrases.en: They announced this year's total order amount.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받은 주문 금액을 모두 합한 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the sum of all orders received.

phrases.en: That company won an order for a large ship.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수주액'의 동사로, 주문을 받는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of '수주액', meaning to receive an order.

explain_en: Receiving an order is '수주' and placing one is '발주', so it helps to remember the two as a pair. '수주액' is the amount of money from orders received, and it often appears in economic news about construction, shipbuilding and exports. The verb is '수주하다'.

examples.en: Our company won a big construction contract.

examples.ko: 그 공장은 새 주문을 수주해서 바빠요.
examples.en: That factory is busy after taking on a new order.

examples.ko: 해외에서 배 열 척을 수주할 예정이에요.
examples.en: They plan to win an order for ten ships from overseas.

examples.ko: 큰 계약을 수주하는 일은 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: Winning a big contract is not easy.

examples.ko: 건설사가 새 다리 공사를 수주하고 기뻐했어요.
examples.en: The construction firm was delighted to win the new bridge job.

examples.ko: 우리는 아직 그 공사를 수주하지 못했어요.
examples.en: We haven't won that construction job yet.

explain: 일을 맡는 쪽이 주문이나 공사를 받을 때 써요. 반대로 일을 맡기는 쪽은 '발주하다'예요. 건설이나 조선 회사 뉴스에서 자주 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 써요.

phrases.en: The factory received a bulk order.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수주하다'를 쉬운 말로 바꾼 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy way to say 수주하다.

phrases.example: 우리 회사가 해외 공사 수주에 성공했어요.
phrases.en: Our company succeeded in winning an overseas construction contract.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수주'를 명사로 써서 일을 따냈다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 수주 as a noun to say a contract was won.

phrases.example: 수주 물량이 많아서 공장이 바쁘게 돌아가요.
phrases.en: The factory is busy because of the large volume of orders.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받아 놓은 주문의 양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the amount of orders already received.

explain_en: Used by the side that takes on the work, receiving an order or construction job. The side that hands out the work uses 발주하다. It shows up in news about construction and shipbuilding firms, and almost never in daily talk.

examples.ko: 이 라면은 전 세계 백 개국에 수출되고 있어요.
examples.en: This ramen is being exported to a hundred countries worldwide.

examples.ko: 한국 화장품이 해외로 수출되는 양이 늘었어요.
examples.en: The amount of Korean cosmetics exported overseas has grown.

examples.ko: 새로 개발한 과일이 바로 수출되면 농민에게 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: If a newly developed fruit is exported right away, it helps farmers.
Rice is inspected before it is exported.

examples.ko: 우리 공장에서 만든 부품이 유럽에 수출되었어요.
examples.en: Parts made at our factory were exported to Europe.

examples.ko: 한국 드라마도 여러 나라에 수출되어 인기를 얻었어요.
examples.en: Korean dramas were also exported to many countries and became popular.

explain: '수출하다'는 나라나 회사가 파는 쪽이고, '수출되다'는 물건이 팔려 나가는 쪽에서 말해요. 반대말은 '수입되다'예요. '수출'과 '수입'은 소리가 비슷해서 헷갈리기 쉬워요.

phrases.en: This fruit is exported overseas.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 어디로 팔려 나가는지 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when saying where the goods are sold to.

phrases.en: This year car exports grew a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '수출'을 써서 수출하는 양이 변했다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun 수출 to say the amount exported has changed.

phrases.example: 우리 회사는 라면을 여러 나라에 수출해요.
phrases.en: Our company exports ramen to many countries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 파는 회사나 나라가 주어일 때는 '수출하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 수출하다 when the company or country doing the selling is the subject.

explain_en: '수출하다' is from the seller's side (a country or company), while '수출되다' is from the viewpoint of the goods being sent out. The opposite is '수입되다'. '수출' and '수입' sound alike, so they are easy to mix up.

examples.en: I want to work at an import-export company.
Trade declined this year, so the port is quiet.
The two countries promised to increase trade.
Imports and exports are very important to a country's economy.
This document is absolutely necessary for importing and exporting.
The scale of trade is growing every year.

explain: '수출'은 물건을 나라 밖으로 내보내는 일, '수입'은 안으로 들여오는 일이에요. 두 가지를 함께 말할 때 '수출입'이라고 하고, 한쪽만 말할 때는 '수출'이나 '수입'을 써요.

phrases.en: I want to get a job at an import-export company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 사고파는 무역 회사를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for a trading company that buys and sells goods across borders.

phrases.en: Imports and exports increased a lot this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '늘다'와 '줄다'를 붙여 변화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Combine with 'increase' or 'decrease' to talk about change.

phrases.en: Exports went up, but imports went down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 가지를 따로 비교할 때는 '수출과 수입'이라고 나눠 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the two words separately when you compare them.

explain_en: '수출' is sending goods out of the country and '수입' is bringing them in. '수출입' covers both together, and for just one side you say '수출' or '수입'.

examples.en: This month's net profit increased compared with last month.

examples.ko: 카페의 순수익을 계산해 보니 생각보다 적었어요.
examples.en: When I calculated the café's net profit, it was less than I thought.

examples.ko: 재료비와 월세를 빼면 순수익이 얼마나 남을까요?
examples.en: After subtracting ingredient costs and rent, how much net profit will be left?
We decided to donate part of the net profit.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 하루 순수익이 십만 원쯤 돼요.
examples.en: This shop makes about 100,000 won in net profit a day.

examples.ko: 매출은 높지만 순수익은 별로 안 남아요.
examples.en: Sales are high, but there isn't much net profit left.

explain: 전체 매출에서 비용을 빼고 실제로 남은 돈이에요. '순이익'도 비슷한 뜻으로 쓰고, 비교하는 말은 '매출'이나 '총수입'이에요.

phrases.example: 이 가게는 한 달 순이익이 삼백만 원이에요.
phrases.en: This shop's net profit is three million won a month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '순수익'과 거의 같은 뜻이고, 회사나 뉴스에서는 '순이익'을 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 순수익; 순이익 is more common in business and news.

phrases.en: Ingredient costs went up, so the net profit decreased.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비용이 늘어 실제로 남는 돈이 적어졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when costs rise and the money actually left over gets smaller.

phrases.en: I subtract the costs from sales to calculate the net profit.
phrases.nuance_ko: '매출'에서 비용을 빼는 계산 이야기를 할 때 자주 붙는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation when talking about subtracting costs from sales.

explain_en: It is the money actually left after subtracting costs from total sales. '순이익' is used with a similar meaning, and the terms to compare it with are '매출' and '총수입'.

examples.ko: 실거래 가격은 인터넷으로 확인할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can check the actual transaction prices on the internet.

examples.ko: 이 아파트 실거래가를 알려 주실 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you tell me the actual sale price of this apartment?
The price confirmed by actual trades was lower than the advertised one.
The advertised price and the actual sale price are very different.

examples.ko: 실거래에 가까운 가격으로 내놓으면 빨리 팔려요.
examples.en: If you list it at a price close to actual trades, it sells fast.
There were no actual trades, yet the asking prices just kept rising.

explain: '실거래가'는 실제로 사고판 가격이고 '호가'는 팔 사람이 부르는 값이에요. 집이나 땅을 사고팔 때 뉴스와 부동산 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I checked the actual transaction price of this house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부르는 값이 아니라 실제로 거래된 가격을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the price actually paid, not the asking price.

phrases.example: 집을 사면 실거래 신고를 해야 해요.
phrases.en: When you buy a house, you have to report the actual transaction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부동산을 사고판 뒤 정부에 알리는 절차를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The procedure of reporting a property sale to the government.

phrases.en: Please look up the actual transaction records online.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 사고판 기록을 확인할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when checking records of real sales.

explain_en: '실거래가' is the price something actually sold for, while '호가' is the price the seller asks. It often comes up in the news and in talk about buying and selling houses or land.

examples.en: Prices are showing a stable trend.
Housing prices have turned stable.
The exchange rate has entered a stable trend.
The market has regained stability this year.
The stable trend continued, so running a shop became easier.
They say government measures are needed to keep things stable.

explain: 가격이나 경기가 크게 오르내리지 않고 차분해지는 흐름을 말하는 뉴스 용어예요. '-세'는 '상승세', '하락세'처럼 흐름을 나타내서 반대로는 '불안정'하거나 '급등세'처럼 말해요. '안정세를 보이다', '안정세를 찾다', '안정세에 접어들다'와 함께 써요.

phrases.en: The market found stability again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흔들리던 것이 차분해질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when something shaky calms down.

phrases.en: House prices have entered a stable phase.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 단계로 들어선다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives a sense of entering a new phase.

phrases.en: The price stability is continuing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안정된 흐름이 계속될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when the stable trend continues.

explain_en: This is a news term for a trend in which prices or the economy calm down instead of swinging a lot. The suffix '-세' marks a trend, as in '상승세' (rising trend) and '하락세' (falling trend). It goes with '안정세를 보이다', '안정세를 찾다' and '안정세에 접어들다'.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 이번 시즌에 큰 약진을 이뤘어요.
examples.en: Our team made a great leap forward this season.

examples.ko: 신인 배우의 약진이 눈에 띄는 한 해였어요.
examples.en: It was a year in which the rising actor's progress stood out.

examples.ko: 경제 약진 덕분에 일자리도 많이 늘었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the economic leap, jobs also increased a lot.

examples.ko: 이 회사의 약진은 새 제품에서 시작됐어요.
examples.en: This company's rapid rise started with a new product.

examples.ko: 그 선수의 약진에 모두가 박수를 보냈어요.
examples.en: Everyone applauded that player's breakthrough.
The overseas advance of Korean films is also remarkable.

explain: 순위, 실적, 인기가 빠르게 좋아지는 모습에 써요. 좋은 변화에 쓰는 말이라 나쁜 일에는 쓰지 않아요. '약진을 거듭하다', '약진이 돋보이다'처럼 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 그 회사는 해마다 약진을 거듭하고 있어요.
phrases.en: That company keeps making rapid advances every year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 성과가 계속 이어질 때 쓰는 뉴스 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A news-style phrase for continued strong progress.

phrases.en: The rookie's rapid rise stood out at this competition.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빠르게 좋아진 모습이 눈에 띈다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise a fast improvement that stands out.

phrases.en: Sales showed a big leap this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실적이 크게 좋아졌을 때 '큰'과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 큰 when results have improved greatly.

explain_en: It is used when rankings, results or popularity improve quickly. Since it is for good changes, it is not used for bad things. It often appears in the news in phrases like '약진을 거듭하다' and '약진이 돋보이다'.

en: to leap; to jump; to spring

examples.ko: 우리 회사가 올해 시장에서 크게 약진했어요.
examples.en: Our company made big strides in the market this year.

examples.ko: 이 선수는 후반기에 약진하며 순위가 올랐어요.
examples.en: This player surged in the second half and moved up in the rankings.

examples.ko: 약진하는 신생 업체들이 점점 많아지고 있어요.
examples.en: The number of fast-rising new companies is gradually growing.

examples.ko: 신인 가수가 한 해 만에 약진해서 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: The rookie singer rose quickly in a year and became a hot topic.
I'll cheer for you to keep advancing in the future too.

examples.ko: 한국 게임이 해외 시장에서 약진한 이유를 알아봤어요.
examples.en: I looked into why Korean games surged in overseas markets.

explain: 주어는 보통 회사, 팀, 선수, 분야처럼 성과가 눈에 보이는 대상이에요. 개인의 작은 일상 성취에는 어색해서, 그럴 때는 '발전하다', '늘다'를 써요. 뉴스나 글에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 우리 팀이 이번 달에 크게 약진했어요.
phrases.en: Our team made a big leap this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로 성과가 빠르게 좋아졌다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense, saying results improved quickly.

phrases.example: 신제품 덕분에 회사가 크게 약진할 거예요.
phrases.en: The company will make a big leap thanks to the new product.
phrases.nuance_ko: '크게'와 함께 쓰면 발전이 크다는 느낌이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 크게, the sense of large progress becomes clear.

phrases.en: Companies in this field are making rapid progress.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 계속 빠르게 성장하는 중이라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say growth is happening right now.

explain_en: The subject is usually something with visible results, such as a company, team, athlete or field. It sounds awkward for small everyday achievements of an individual; in that case use '발전하다' or '늘다'. It is common in news and writing.

examples.en: That player receives a salary of over a hundred million won.
I have debts in the hundred-million range, so my heart is heavy.
These days in Seoul, jeonse deposits of over a hundred million won are common.
News of a contract worth over a hundred million won came out.
I heard there are even YouTubers earning over a hundred million won.

examples.ko: 그 집은 억대를 훌쩍 넘는 가격이에요.
examples.en: That house is priced well over a hundred million won.

explain: '억' 단위의 큰 돈을 말해요. 원 단위로 보면 1억 원부터 9억 원대까지를 뜻하고, '억대 연봉', '억대 계약'처럼 자주 써요. 돈이 더 크면 '십억대'나 '조 단위'처럼 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 회사는 억대 연봉을 주는 것으로 유명해요.
phrases.en: That company is famous for paying a salary in the hundreds of millions of won.
phrases.nuance_ko: '억대'가 연봉 같은 소득 앞에 붙어서 1억 원대에서 9억 원대까지의 큰 수입을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '억대' goes before income words like salary to mean earnings in the range of 100 million to under 1 billion won.
phrases.en_equiv: a salary of hundreds of millions of won

phrases.en: I heard that singer signed a contract worth hundreds of millions of won.
phrases.nuance_ko: '계약' 앞에 붙여서 계약 금액이 억 원 단위로 크다는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before 'contract' to say the contract amount is in the hundreds of millions of won.
phrases.en_equiv: a contract worth hundreds of millions

phrases.en: That person has assets worth hundreds of millions of won.
phrases.nuance_ko: '재산'과 함께 써서 가진 돈이나 집의 값이 억 원 단위라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 'property/assets' to say what someone owns is worth in the hundreds of millions of won.

explain_en: It refers to large sums in the unit of '억' (hundred million). In won, that is from 100 million up to the 900-million range, as in '억대 연봉' (salary in the hundred-million range) and '억대 계약'. For larger amounts people say '십억대' or '조 단위'.

examples.ko: 관아로 찾아가는 사람들이 얼추 백 명이나 됐어요.
examples.en: The people heading to the government office numbered about a hundred.

examples.ko: 공연장에 사람이 얼추 천 명은 왔어요.
examples.en: Roughly a thousand people came to the concert hall.
My homework is almost done.

examples.ko: 얼추 계산해 봐도 십만 원은 넘어요.
examples.en: Even by a rough calculation, it's over a hundred thousand won.

examples.ko: 여기서 역까지 얼추 십 분쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes roughly ten minutes from here to the station.

examples.ko: 그 사람 나이가 저랑 얼추 비슷해요.
examples.en: He is about the same age as me.

explain: 정확하지는 않지만 거의 맞는 수나 정도를 말할 때 써요. '대략'과 비슷한데 더 편한 대화 느낌이 있어요. 숫자 앞에서는 '얼추 백 명', '비슷하다·끝나다' 같은 말 앞에서는 '거의 다'라는 뜻이 돼요.

phrases.en: The two people are roughly the same height.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정확히 같지는 않지만 거의 비슷하다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means almost the same, though not exactly.

phrases.en: My homework is pretty much done.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 거의 끝나 갈 때 쓰는 편한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual expression for when something is almost finished.

phrases.en: The number I calculated is about right.
phrases.nuance_ko: 완전히 정확하진 않아도 거의 맞다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means close to correct even if not perfectly exact.

explain_en: It means a number or degree that isn't exact but is nearly right. It is like '대략' but has a more casual, conversational feel. Before a number it means 'about', and before words like '비슷하다' (similar) or '끝나다' (end) it means 'almost'.

examples.en: This savings account has an annual interest rate of 3 percent.
Check the annual interest rate before you take out a loan.
The annual interest rate differs a little from bank to bank.
If you deposit 1 million won at 5 percent a year, you get 50,000 won in a year.
A card loan has a high annual rate, and there are fees too.
I compared annual interest rates and then opened an account.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '금리'나 '이자'라고 더 많이 말해요. 은행 상품 설명이나 계약서에서 '연 3%'처럼 숫자와 함께 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: This product has a high annual interest rate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이자가 많은지 적은지 말할 때 '높다/낮다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 높다/낮다 to say whether the interest is high or low.

phrases.en: I signed up for a savings account with a 3 percent annual interest rate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숫자와 함께 은행 상품을 설명할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with a number when describing bank products.

phrases.en: Interest rates have gone up lately, so my interest has grown.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '연이율'보다 '금리'를 더 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily conversation, 금리 is used more often than 연이율.

explain_en: In daily conversation people more often say '금리' or '이자'. 연이율 appears in bank product descriptions and contracts, usually alongside numbers like '연 3%'.

en: to be petty; to be small

examples.en: Small businesses with little capital find it hard to get loans.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 규모가 영세해서 직원이 두 명뿐이에요.
examples.en: This shop is so small-scale that it has only two employees.
The government gave support money to small-scale merchants.

examples.ko: 회사가 너무 영세해서 월급이 늦게 나올 때도 있어요.
examples.en: The company is so small that salaries are sometimes late.

examples.ko: 영세하게 시작했지만 지금은 직원이 백 명이에요.
examples.en: It started out small, but now it has a hundred employees.
Most of the factories in my neighborhood are small and poorly funded.

explain: 규모가 작고 자본이 넉넉하지 않은 가게나 업체, 상인에게 써요. '영세한 업체', '영세 상인'처럼 쓰고, 사람 개인이 가난할 때는 '가난하다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 영세한 업체를 돕는 정책이 새로 나왔어요.
phrases.en: A new policy to help small businesses was announced.
phrases.nuance_ko: '영세한'을 명사 앞에 붙여 규모가 작고 돈이 부족한 회사를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put '영세한' before a noun to refer to a company that is small and short on money.

phrases.example: 영세 상인들이 가게 문을 닫고 있어요.
phrases.en: Small merchants are closing their shops.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 가게를 하는 상인을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for merchants who run small shops.

phrases.en: Our company is still small and short of funds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 서술할 때는 회사나 가게가 주어로 와요.
phrases.nuance_en: In a plain statement the subject is a company or shop.
phrases.en_equiv: is small and poor in capital

explain_en: It describes shops, businesses or merchants that are small and short on capital, as in '영세한 업체' or '영세 상인'. For a person who is poor, use '가난하다' instead.

examples.ko: 요즘 환율이 하루에도 몇 번씩 오르락내리락해요.
examples.en: These days the exchange rate goes up and down several times a day.
My grades keep going up and down, and I'm worried.
The baby's temperature went up and down all night.
There are days when my mood goes up and down.

examples.ko: 저 아이들은 왜 계단을 오르락내리락하고 있어요?
examples.en: Why are those kids going up and down the stairs?
When prices fluctuate, it's hard to keep a household ledger.

explain: 실제로 위아래로 움직이는 것과 값이나 상태가 변하는 것 모두에 써요. '변동하다'보다 구어적이고, 좋았다 나빴다 하는 불안정한 느낌이 있어요. '기분이 오르락내리락하다'는 감정 기복이 있다는 뜻으로 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: My mood went up and down yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지나간 일의 변화를 말하는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, for describing a change that already happened.

phrases.en: Prices aren't fluctuating these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 값이나 상태가 안정되어 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means that a price or condition is stable.

phrases.en: Stock prices often rise and fall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 더 짧고 글에도 자주 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shorter, similar word that also appears often in writing.

explain_en: It covers both physical up-and-down movement and values or conditions that keep changing. It is more colloquial than '변동하다' and has a feel of instability, good then bad. '기분이 오르락내리락하다' is a common way to say your moods swing.

examples.ko: 이번 달 물가 오름폭이 지난달보다 커졌어요.
examples.en: This month's price increase is bigger than last month's.

examples.ko: 집값 오름폭이 조금 줄었다는 뉴스가 나왔어요.
examples.en: There was news that the rise in housing prices has slowed a little.
The rise in the stock price wasn't as big as I expected.

examples.ko: 기온 오름폭이 커서 옷 입기가 힘들어요.
examples.en: The temperature rises so much that it's hard to decide what to wear.

examples.ko: 전기 요금 오름폭이 얼마나 될지 궁금해요.
examples.en: I wonder how much electricity rates will go up.
The raise in my salary this year is small, so I'm disappointed.

explain: 물가, 집값, 금리처럼 숫자가 오른 정도를 말할 때 쓰고, '오름폭이 크다/줄다'로 자주 말해요. '상승폭'과 같은 뜻이고, 반대는 '하락폭'이에요.

phrases.en: This year the rise in interest rates is large.
phrases.nuance_ko: 많이 올랐다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to say something rose by a lot.

phrases.en: The rise in prices has narrowed a little.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계속 오르지만 오르는 정도가 작아질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something is still rising but by less than before.

phrases.en: The rise in house prices has become smaller.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오름폭'과 뜻이 같고 뉴스에서 더 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as the headword, but heard more often in the news.

explain_en: It is used for how much numbers such as prices, housing costs or interest rates went up, as in '오름폭이 크다/줄다'. It means the same as '상승폭', and its opposite is '하락폭'.

en: unpaid tab; amount owed on credit

examples.ko: 이번 달 외상값은 다음 주까지 꼭 갚을게요.
examples.en: I'll definitely pay this month's tab by next week.
The shop owner called about the unpaid tab.

examples.ko: 외상값이 쌓여서 이제는 더 못 사요.
examples.en: The tab has piled up, so I can't buy any more now.
My father collected the outstanding bill from a client.
Please settle the whole tab at once at the end of the month.

examples.ko: 친구에게 빌린 돈이 아니라 식당 외상값이에요.
examples.en: It's not money borrowed from a friend, it's a restaurant tab.

explain: '외상'은 물건을 먼저 받고 돈은 나중에 내는 거래예요. 그래서 '외상으로 사다', '외상값을 갚다/받다'처럼 짝지어 써요. 가게에 '외상 사절'이라고 써 붙이기도 해요.

phrases.en: When I get my pay, I will pay off my tab.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 나중에 내는 상황에서 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for paying a debt owed on credit.

phrases.en: I didn't have money, so I bought snacks on credit.
phrases.nuance_ko: '외상값' 대신 거래 방식을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the way of buying rather than the amount owed.

phrases.en: The shop owner came to collect the money owed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 받는 가게 주인의 입장에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the shop owner's side, the one who receives the money.

explain_en: '외상' is buying first and paying later, so it pairs as '외상으로 사다' and '외상값을 갚다/받다'. Some shops put up a sign saying '외상 사절' (no credit).

examples.ko: 그 나라는 외채가 너무 많아서 어려움을 겪어요.
examples.en: That country is struggling because its foreign debt is too large.

examples.ko: 정부가 외채를 갚기 위해 노력하고 있어요.
examples.en: The government is working to repay its foreign debt.
The country's economy was shaken by the foreign debt problem.

examples.ko: 외채에 대한 걱정이 점점 커지고 있어요.
examples.en: Worry about foreign debt is growing little by little.
They say it is important to reduce foreign debt.
The foreign debt repayment schedule was announced yesterday.

explain: 나라나 기업이 외국에서 빌린 빚을 말하고, 경제 뉴스나 사회 수업에서 자주 나와요. '외채를 갚다', '외채가 늘다'처럼 써요. 개인의 빚 이야기에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: The government paid off all of its foreign debt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빌린 돈을 돌려준다는 뜻으로 가장 많이 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, meaning to repay the borrowed money.

phrases.example: 몇 년 사이에 그 나라의 외채가 많이 늘었어요.
phrases.en: That country's foreign debt has grown a lot in a few years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라의 빚이 많아진다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say a country's debt is growing.

phrases.en: The news explained the foreign debt problem in detail.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경제 뉴스나 사회 수업에서 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase seen in economic news and social studies classes.

explain_en: It means debt that a country or company has borrowed from abroad, and appears often in economic news and social studies. It is used as '외채를 갚다' (repay) and '외채가 늘다' (grow). It is not used for an individual's personal debt.

examples.ko: 올여름 실내 온도가 40도에 육박해서 에어컨을 하루 종일 켰어요.
examples.en: This summer the indoor temperature neared 40 degrees, so I kept the air conditioner on all day.

examples.ko: 신규 가입자 수가 백만 명에 육박한다는 보도가 나왔어요.
examples.en: A report said the number of new subscribers is approaching one million.
This month's living expenses are almost as much as my salary.

examples.ko: 올해 관광객이 천만 명에 육박할 것으로 보여요.
examples.en: The number of tourists this year is expected to approach ten million.
The inflation rate came close to 5 percent.

examples.ko: 우리 팀 점수가 상대 팀 점수에 육박하고 있어요.
examples.en: Our team's score is closing in on the other team's score.

explain: '~에 육박하다' 형태로 쓰고, 온도·인원·금액처럼 숫자로 나타내는 것이 어떤 수치에 거의 닿을 때 써요. 뉴스 문장에서 많이 보이고, 일상에서는 '거의 ~예요'라고 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.example: 이번 달 판매량이 만 개에 육박했어요.
phrases.en: Sales this month came close to ten thousand units.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 숫자가 어떤 수치에 거의 닿았다고 뉴스처럼 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, used news-style to say a figure nearly reached a number.

phrases.en: Heat approaching 35 degrees is continuing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸며서 '거의 그 수치에 가까운'이라는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form that adds the sense of 'nearly reaching that figure' to the following noun.

phrases.en: The participants number nearly a thousand.
phrases.nuance_ko: '육박하다'보다 쉽고 일상 대화에서 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, more natural everyday alternative to 육박하다.

explain_en: It is used in the pattern '~에 육박하다' when something measured in numbers, such as temperature, people or money, almost reaches a figure. You see it a lot in news sentences, while in daily talk people often just say '거의 ~예요' (it's almost ~).

examples.en: I took out a loan from the bank to buy a house.
I looked into the terms of the government loan.
I opened a shop with a loan, and paying it back is hard.
You can pay back the loan money in monthly installments.
A startup loan requires a lot of application documents.

examples.ko: 융자가 거절돼서 다른 은행에 가 봤어요.
examples.en: My loan was rejected, so I tried another bank.

explain: 은행이나 정부에서 돈을 빌리는 일을 말하고, 일상에서는 '대출'이 더 흔해요. '융자'는 주택, 창업, 정책 자금 같은 이야기에서 자주 나오고 '융자를 받다/신청하다/갚다'로 써요.

phrases.en: I'm looking into a bank loan.
phrases.nuance_ko: '융자'와 같은 뜻이고 일상에서는 이쪽이 더 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 융자 and more common in daily life.

phrases.en: I'm paying back the loan money in monthly installments.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빌린 돈 자체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the borrowed money itself.

phrases.en: I prepared documents to apply for a startup loan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 빌리려고 공식적으로 요청할 때 써요. 앞에 창업, 주택 같은 말을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when formally applying to borrow money. Words like 창업 or 주택 often go before it.

explain_en: It refers to borrowing money from a bank or the government, and '대출' is more common in daily talk. '융자' often appears for housing, startup or policy funds, used as '융자를 받다/신청하다/갚다'.

examples.ko: 병원에 오래 다녀서 의료비가 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: I went to the hospital for a long time, so the medical bills were high.
I bought insurance to reduce my medical expense burden.
The government decided to support medical costs for seniors.

examples.ko: 한 해 동안 쓴 의료비는 세금 공제를 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Medical expenses from the year can qualify for a tax deduction.
Please keep your medical expense receipts safe.
In the US, medical costs are much higher than in Korea.

explain: 치료, 약, 검사에 드는 돈을 크게 묶어 말할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '병원비'나 '치료비'를 더 편하게 말해요. '의료비 부담', '의료비 지원'처럼 뉴스와 보험 이야기에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The burden of medical expenses is so big that I'm worried.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치료에 드는 돈이 힘들 때 뉴스나 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news and talk when treatment costs are hard to bear.

phrases.en: The government increased medical expense support for children.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라나 단체가 병원에 드는 돈을 도와줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the state or an organization helps pay medical costs.

phrases.en: I caught a cold, so the hospital bill came to quite a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의료비'보다 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more casual everyday word than 의료비.

explain_en: It groups together the money spent on treatment, medicine and tests. In everyday talk '병원비' or '치료비' is more casual. It often appears in the news and insurance talk, as in '의료비 부담' and '의료비 지원'.

examples.en: We will donate all the profit from the event.
This year's profit grew a lot compared to last year.
We decided to share the profit with the employees.
We use part of the profit for scholarships.
We bought books with the profit made at the bazaar.
You have to subtract the tax from the profit first.

explain: '이익'이 넓은 말이라면 '이익금'은 실제로 남은 돈의 액수를 가리켜서, 기부하거나 나누는 상황에서 잘 나와요. 비슷한 말로 '수익', '이윤'이 있어요. 반대되는 상황은 '손해'나 '적자'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I split the profit equally with my business partners.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남은 돈을 여러 사람이 나누는 상황에서 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for dividing leftover money among people.

phrases.en: This year the shop had a lot of profit left over.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비용을 빼고 실제로 돈이 남았다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means money actually remained after costs were subtracted.

phrases.en: We gave all the proceeds from the bazaar to the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이익금'과 비슷한 말이고, 행사나 판매로 번 돈을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A near-synonym often used for money earned from events or sales.

explain_en: While '이익' is a broad word, '이익금' points to the actual amount of money left over, so it shows up in contexts like donating or dividing it. Similar words are '수익' and '이윤'. The opposite situation is called '손해' or '적자'.

examples.en: Bus fares will be reduced from next month.
When interest rates are cut, loan interest goes down.
I saw an ad saying the price had been cut.

examples.ko: 인하된 가격에 물건을 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can buy the item at the reduced price.
I wonder whether taxes will be cut.
I was disappointed that electricity rates weren't cut.

explain: 가격·요금·금리·세금처럼 숫자가 내려갈 때만 써요. 반대말은 '인상되다'인데, 발음이 비슷해서 헷갈리니까 '인하=아래, 인상=위'로 기억하세요. 가게에서는 보통 '싸졌다', '할인'이라고 말해요.

phrases.en: The government lowers taxes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '인하되다'의 능동형으로, 내리는 쪽이 주어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form; the one lowering is the subject.

phrases.en: I heard the news about the price cut.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 광고에서 명사로 자주 보이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun phrase often seen in news and ads.

phrases.en: Interest rates go down.
phrases.nuance_ko: '인하되다'보다 쉬운 말로, 숫자가 낮아질 때 두루 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word than 인하되다 for numbers getting lower.

explain_en: Only for numbers that go down: prices, fees, interest rates, taxes. The opposite is '인상되다', and the two sound alike, so remember 인하 = down, 인상 = up. In shops people just say '싸졌다' or '할인'.

p.n: 절감되다 is for costs saved, not a price being set lower.

en: to reduce; to cut; to bring down

examples.en: The store is cutting its prices.
The bank lowered the interest rate.
If you lower the price, customers increase.
They are looking for ways to cut taxes.
They plan to lower the fee.
We are selling at the reduced price.

explain: 가격, 이자, 세금 같은 숫자를 내릴 때 써요. 반대말은 '인상하다'예요. '값을 내리다'보다 격식 있는 말이에요.

phrases.en: Bus fares will be reduced from next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 내렸는지보다 값이 내려진 결과가 중요할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the result of the price being lowered matters more than who lowered it.

phrases.example: 이번 주에 가격 인하 행사를 해요.
phrases.en: There is a price cut event this week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '인하'를 붙여 광고나 안내문에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun form often seen in ads and notices.

phrases.en: The company decided to reduce the fee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인하하기로 결정했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means that someone has decided to make a cut.

explain_en: Use it when lowering numbers like prices, interest, or taxes. The opposite is '인상하다'. It is more formal than '값을 내리다'.

p.n: Prices are lowered, so 줄이다 is unnatural here.

examples.ko: 이번 달에는 잉여 자금이 조금 생겼어요.
examples.en: This month some surplus funds came up.

examples.ko: 회사의 잉여 인력을 다른 부서로 옮겼어요.
examples.en: The company moved its surplus staff to another department.
Surplus farm products are sometimes sold at a low price.
I saved the surplus that was left over after spending.

examples.ko: 잉여가 생기지 않도록 주문량을 잘 맞춰요.
examples.en: We adjust the order amount well so that no excess builds up.

examples.ko: 잉여 예산은 다음 달로 넘기기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to carry the excess budget over to next month.

explain: 필요한 만큼 쓰고도 남은 것을 말해요. '나머지'나 '남은 것'은 일상 말이고, '잉여'는 경제·회사 글에서 '잉여 인력', '잉여 생산물'처럼 써요. 인터넷에서는 할 일 없는 사람을 놀리는 말로도 쓰니 조심하세요.

phrases.en: They sold the surplus crops cheaply.
phrases.nuance_ko: 필요한 만큼 쓰고도 남은 농산물을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to farm products left over after meeting demand.

phrases.en: We carried the surplus funds over to next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사나 단체가 쓰고 남은 돈을 부르는 회계 쪽 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An accounting term for money left over after spending.

phrases.en: We store the surplus power and use it later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓰고 남은 전기를 말할 때 쓰는 기술·경제 쪽 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A technical/economic collocation for leftover electricity.

explain_en: It refers to what is left over after using what was needed. 나머지 and 남은 것 are everyday words, while 잉여 appears in economic and business writing, as in 잉여 인력 and 잉여 생산물. Online it is also used to tease someone with nothing to do, so be careful.

en: as much as; no less than

examples.ko: 그 책은 자그마치 천 쪽이나 돼요.
examples.en: That book is no less than a thousand pages.

examples.ko: 오늘 모인 사람이 자그마치 오천 명이래요.
examples.en: They say as many as five thousand people gathered today.
This bag costs a whopping three million won.

examples.ko: 그는 혼자서 자그마치 열 시간을 걸었어요.
examples.en: He walked for a full ten hours all by himself.

examples.ko: 시험 준비에 자그마치 일 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: Preparing for the exam took a whole year.

examples.ko: 이 나무는 자그마치 오백 살이 넘었어요.
examples.en: This tree is over five hundred years old, no less.

explain: 수나 양, 시간이 생각보다 많아서 놀랍다는 느낌을 강조할 때 써요. 뒤에는 숫자나 단위가 오고 '고작'과는 반대의 느낌이에요. '자그마하다(작다)'와 모양이 비슷하지만 뜻은 반대라서 헷갈리지 않게 조심하세요.

phrases.example: 이 일을 하는 데 자그마치 십 년이나 걸렸어요.
phrases.en: It took no less than ten years to do this.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자그마치' 뒤에 숫자와 '이나'를 붙이면 놀라움이 더 잘 드러나요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding a number and 이나 after it brings out the surprise.

phrases.example: 올해 가격이 자그마치 두 배가 됐어요.
phrases.en: This year the price doubled, no less.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 늘어난 정도를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to stress a large increase.

phrases.en: As many as a thousand people came to the venue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 수가 예상보다 많아서 놀랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the number of people is surprisingly large.
phrases.en_equiv: as many as a thousand people

explain_en: It stresses surprise that a number, amount or length of time is larger than expected, and is followed by a number or unit. It feels like the opposite of '고작' (a mere). It looks like '자그마하다' (small), but the meaning is the reverse, so be careful not to mix them up.

examples.ko: 작은 가게를 열 자본금을 모으고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm saving up the capital to open a small shop.

examples.ko: 회사를 만들 때 자본금이 얼마나 필요해요?
examples.en: How much capital do you need to start a company?
We didn't have enough capital, so we decided to take investment.
That company's capital is fifty million won.
I invested with a friend to increase the capital.
It's hard to start a business without capital.

explain: 가게를 열 때 쓰는 돈은 일상에서 '창업 자금'이나 '밑천'이라고 해요. 회사를 세울 때 법적으로 등록하는 돈일 때 '자본금'이라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I borrowed startup funds from the bank.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 가게나 사업을 시작할 때 쓰는 돈을 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday way to talk about money for starting a shop or business.

phrases.en: I need a little money to start my business.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자본금'보다 쉽고 편한 말로, 무언가를 시작하는 데 드는 돈을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plainer, more casual word than 자본금 for the money needed to get started.

phrases.en: I couldn't open the shop because I lacked capital.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자본금'과 가장 자주 같이 쓰는 말이에요. 돈이 모자랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A very common pairing with 자본금 when the money is not enough.

explain_en: Everyday talk calls money for opening a shop '창업 자금' or '밑천'. '자본금' is used for the money legally registered when a company is founded.

en: rich man; man of property; man of fortune

examples.en: He is a wealthy man who made money from real estate.
Wealthy people get investment advice separately.

examples.ko: 한 자산가가 학교에 큰 기부금을 냈어요.
examples.en: A wealthy man donated a large sum to the school.
I am not wealthy, but I save diligently.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 자산가를 위한 세금 이야기가 나왔어요.
examples.en: The news had a story about taxes for the wealthy.
I heard he grew up without worries as a rich man's son.

explain: '부자'가 일상에서 가장 흔하고, '자산가'는 땅, 건물, 주식처럼 재산이 많은 사람을 말할 때 조금 격식 있게 써요. 뉴스나 금융 이야기에서 자주 들려요.

phrases.example: 저 건물 주인은 아주 큰 부자예요.
phrases.en: The owner of that building is very rich.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 가장 흔한 말이고, '자산가'보다 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common everyday word, more casual than '자산가'.

phrases.en: He became a man of wealth through stock investing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재산이 많은 사람이 되었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means becoming a person with substantial assets.

phrases.example: 젊은 자산가들이 새로운 투자 방법을 찾고 있어요.
phrases.en: Young wealthy people are looking for new ways to invest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 경제 기사에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often found in news and economic articles.

explain_en: '부자' is the everyday word; '자산가' sounds a bit more formal and fits people with lots of property, buildings or stocks. You often hear it in news and finance talk.

en: to be low; to be low-pitched

examples.ko: 올해 우리 가게의 판매 실적이 저조해요.
examples.en: Our shop's sales results are poor this year.
Turnout for the event was far too low.
I worry when my exam scores are poor.

examples.ko: 요즘 우리 팀의 득점이 저조한 편이에요.
examples.en: Our team's scoring has been sluggish lately.
The response was weak, so we scaled down the event.

examples.ko: 출석이 저조하지 않도록 신경 써 주세요.
examples.en: Please make sure attendance doesn't turn out low.

explain: 성적, 실적, 참여율처럼 숫자로 보이는 결과가 기대보다 낮을 때 써요. 사람 자체를 가리키지 않고 '참여가 저조하다'처럼 일의 결과를 말해요. '부진하다'와 비슷한 상황에서 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: The player is worried because of the poor results.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기대보다 낮은 성적이나 결과를 앞에서 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes results that are lower than expected.

phrases.en: This month's sales are not low.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기대만큼 나쁘지 않다고 부정으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form, saying that results are not as low as feared.

phrases.en: Participation is low, so we are preparing the event again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과가 낮은 이유를 말하면서 다음 이야기를 이어 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives low results as the reason for what comes next.

explain_en: Used when a measurable result such as grades, performance, or turnout is lower than hoped. It describes the outcome of something, as in '참여가 저조하다', not a person. It's used in situations similar to 부진하다.

examples.ko: 검사에서 걸린 불량 제품은 전량 폐기했어요.
examples.en: All the defective products found in the inspection were discarded.

examples.ko: 주문한 물건 전량이 오늘 아침에 도착했어요.
examples.en: The whole amount of the goods I ordered arrived this morning.

examples.ko: 손님이 남은 빵 전량을 사 가셨어요.
examples.en: A customer bought all of the remaining bread.
We'll sell all of the stock at a discount starting tomorrow.

examples.ko: 전량으로 계약하면 가격을 더 깎아 준대요.
examples.en: They say they'll lower the price more if you contract for the whole amount.

examples.ko: 이번에 수확한 쌀은 전량 수출될 예정이에요.
examples.en: All of the rice harvested this time is going to be exported.

explain: '전량 폐기', '전량 수입', '전량 판매'처럼 물건의 양 전체를 말하는 업무·뉴스 말투예요. 일상에서는 '전부', '다', '몽땅'이라고 해요. 사람이나 시간에는 쓰지 않고 물건의 양에만 써요.

phrases.en: This fruit is all imported.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 물건을 전부 다른 나라에서 들여올 때 쓰는 업무·뉴스 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A business or news phrase for when an item is brought in entirely from abroad.

phrases.en: They recalled all of the defective products.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제 있는 물건을 모두 거두어들일 때 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in the news when all problem items are taken back.

phrases.en: All the items I ordered have arrived.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전량'은 딱딱하고, 일상에서는 '전부'나 '다'를 더 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '전량' is formal; in daily life '전부' or '다' sounds more natural.

explain_en: It is a business and news style word for the whole quantity of goods, as in '전량 폐기', '전량 수입' and '전량 판매'. In daily talk people say '전부', '다' or '몽땅'. It is not used for people or time, only for quantities of things.
